prompt:
A sharp top-down photograph of 8 white domino tiles laid end to end in a single horizontal row (a 'domino train') on the dark slate tabletop of a neighbourhood CAFE domino club. Two rules must BOTH hold:
1) MATCHING: where two tiles touch, the pip numbers on the two touching ends must be EQUAL (the normal domino train rule) - so the right half of each tile matches the left half of the next tile.
2) TOTAL: the grand total of ALL the pips on all 8 tiles (adding up both halves of every tile) must equal EXACTLY 63.
Each tile is a standard domino: a white rectangle split by a centre line into two square halves, each half showing 0 to 6 black pips in the usual dice arrangement. Lay the 8 tiles in a straight left-to-right row, touching end to end, all fully visible and non-overlapping. No numerals, text or labels anywhere - only pip dots.
easy_question: Never mind how well it is drawn. Does this picture show cafe domino-club train of white domino tiles laid end-to-end on a dark slate tabletop under a match-and-total rule? A realistic photo, an illustration, a schematic or a clean diagram ALL count as yes. Answer NO only if the image instead shows just a blank card or plain panel that prints an answer with none of that shown, or shows something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.

Does that dividing line run ACROSS the tile (so the two halves are an upper half and a lower half), or does it run UP AND DOWN the tile (so the two halves are a left half and a right half)? Answer with exactly one word: across or updown.
